Sean —

Team —

Summary: Finly (payments) reporting sustained latency + increased 5xx. Customer asserts potential SLA breach (99.5% availability). They are sensitive — checkout flow impacted. Attachments: logs_20260225.zip from customer.

Immediate asks:
- Steph: please prioritize root-cause investigation (model runtimes, shard overheating, autoscale failures, routing fallbacks). Check for degraded GPU host(s), queue depth anomalies, and any prefix cache invalidations.
- Markus: compute quick estimate of affected request % and duration windows so we can model a provisional credit amount if SLA looks impacted. Use the attached sampling but correlate with our internal telemetry (token-level latencies, queue depth).

Communication plan: aim to provide Finly with a remediation timeline + provisional credit estimate within 4 business hours. If we confirm an SLA miss, we will propose credit per contract section 5.2 and outline remediation steps + timeline for recurrence prevention.

Steph — can you confirm whether this is isolated to hosted api region us-west-2 or broader?

Monica

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Finly incident — logs attached, SLA/credits heads-up

Monica / team —

Investigation update (initial):
- Scope: elevated latency and 5xx observed across us-west-2 and us-east-1 for routes tied to model-id: rwd-gpt-13b-v2 and a custom quantized variant used by Finly. Not limited to a single region.
- Root cause hypothesis: a kernel regression in the recent runtime micro-release (v2.8.3) causes suboptimal thread utilization during heavy prefix cache churn; combined with a micro-burst in checkout traffic we saw queue growth and fallback behavior leading to increased 5xx.
- Mitigation performed: rolled back runtime to v2.8.1 on impacted worker pools and drained hot queues; enabled conservative autoscale to add temporary capacity. Error rates dropped to baseline within ~45 minutes after rollback.

Next steps:
- Create incident postmortem and full timeline (I started a doc).
- Markus — please work with telemetry to compute the window where availability dipped below SLA and provide estimated impacted request volume. Include per-minute availability for 2026-02-25 07:15–10:30 PT.
- Ops: schedule a canary rollout of v2.8.3 with additional profiling hooks after root cause fix.

Attachments: incident_postmortem_v1.pdf (work-in-progress)

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Rachel Chen <rachel.chen@finly.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Service Impact Review & Remediation Plan — Finly (SLA Credit / Fix Timeline)

Rachel — thanks for your patience. Quick summary and proposed remediation / commercial fix:  

What happened (TL;DR): a recent runtime micro-release (v2.8.3) introduced a regression under certain cache-churn patterns which, combined with a traffic microburst, caused elevated latencies and temporary 5xx. We rolled back impacted pools to v2.8.1 and restored normal error rates in ~45 minutes. Full timeline + RCA attached.

Proposed immediate remediation:
- Technical: permanent fix to kernel scheduling in next patch (ETA: 10 business days), plus a constrained canary rollout with additional profiling. We'll also add a temporary autoscale policy for your routes to provide burst capacity while the patch lands.
- Operational: provide you with a dedicated incident postmortem and an itemized remediation plan within 3 business days.
- Commercial: provisional SLA credit. Based on our early telemetry, availability dipped below 99.5% for an ~28-minute window impacting approximately 0.9% of your monthly request volume. Per contract section 5.2, we propose a credit of 10% of February hosting fees for the affected service tier. Attached is a simple credit calculation workbook: credit_calculation_FINLY.xlsx. This is provisional pending Markus's final numbers.

Requested next steps from Finly:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the remediation & credit approach (we can formalize via amendment).
2) If accepted, we'll issue a draft amendment for signature and apply the provisional credit to your March invoice within 5 business days of agreement.

If you'd prefer escalation to our VP of Product / CTO for faster contract amendment, we can do that — let me know.

Apologies again for the outage; we consider this high priority.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
